deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 22% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 18% last year; 17%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 30% (3 years ago 51%, falling) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $30 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 30% (3 years ago 35%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $683.0B, up 72% from a year ago — about 2.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $69.6B, up 13% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 17%/yr over 3 years and 14%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 47% vs a 5-year range of 41–47% (median 45%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $48.0B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($21.0B buybacks + $27.0B dividends) = 1.3% of the company's market value. Share count down 0.3% from a year ago (about flat).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $24.20, up 3% in 90 days (up 2% in the last 30); 25 analysts raised, 3 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $20.01, up 1% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 25 analysts raised, 3 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers
deeper.text: Compared with 7 peers (ORCL, GOOGL, AMZN, CRM, ADBE, NOW, IBM): sales growth over the last 12 months 18% vs a median of 15%; operating margin 47% vs 26%; price/sales 10.6× vs 3.5×.

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Agents and infra 83% of sales, up 25%; Devices and consumer 17% of sales, down 3%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $74.8M, 96% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

deeper.title: New risk factors
deeper.text: 4 new risk-factor headings vs last year's annual report, e.g. “Our cloud and AI strategy requires substantial investments and depends on evolving customer demand, technologi…”; “Our success depends on our ability to develop, deliver, and maintain competitive cloud-based and AI products a…”.

note.headline: Microsoft rebounds 1.65% to 492.5, back above support; hold, swing entry triggered

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and margins keep improving, but free cash flow has fallen while heavy spending continues, so the stock looks cheap against its own history and expensive on cash flow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold and add only lower. Swing: enter, because the price closed back above the 491.22 trigger set in the last note.
summary.act_at: Swing entry 491.22, stop 480.69, target 503.99; long-term add at 475.73

note.happening: Microsoft rose 1.65% to 492.5. That put it back above the top of its 486.0–491.22 support zone, a few days after it broke below that zone. The only news since the last note is a CNBC report of a government official warning of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages, and the report does not name Microsoft. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
note.business: The latest filing, dated 2026-10-28, shows a business that is still speeding up. Quarterly revenue grew 18.8% from a year earlier, compared with 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Analysts raised next-year earnings per share to 24.2, up 2.2% in 30 days. The weak point is cash. Trailing free cash flow (cash left after capital spending) fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the filings say each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, down from 51¢ three years ago. In other words, the heavy spending has not paid back yet. That spending is the real business risk. Demand and margins are not at risk on current data. The balance sheet is not at risk either: net cash is 29.0B and the share count shrank 0.27% over the year. The outage news and the tech-sector fear flagged by the macro read affect sentiment, not Microsoft's revenue or margins.

worth.text: The valuation methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow model starts from today's 60.0B of free cash flow, assumes growth fades to 3% by year 10, and discounts at 10.0%. It gives 180.81 to 288.62 per share, with 218.43 in the middle. For the cash-flow model to justify today's price, free cash flow would have to start growing about 40.0% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, and even that gives only 343.43. Measured against its own past, the stock is cheap. Its price-to-sales ratio of 10.6 is at the 28th percentile of its own 5-year range, and that history gives 475.73 to 592.92, with 535.43 in the middle. Against peers it is expensive: the peer median price-to-sales is 3.4. Earnings multiples sit in between, at 25.7 times trailing earnings and 20.4 times next year's earnings. The gap between methods comes down to one input: whether the shrunken 60.0B cash base is temporary. I use the own-history range from 475.73 to 535.43, because current earnings and margins support it. The cash-flow figures are the downside reminder if that bet fails.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so next-year earnings (estimate 24.2) are the right basis for value, not today's cash flow.

bull: Revenue growth picked up to 18.8% year over year, from 18.3% two quarters ago, and operating margin rose to 47.1% from 46.27%.
Analysts raised next-year EPS to 24.2, up 2.2% in 30 days. That puts the stock at 20.4 times next year's earnings.
Price-to-sales sits at the 28th percentile of its own 5-year range, and the price is close to the 475.73 low end of its historical fair range.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the filings say returns on investment dropped to 30¢ per dollar from 51¢.
The cash-flow model's base value is 218.43, and today's price requires about 40.0% starting cash-flow growth.
Price-to-sales is 10.6 versus a peer median of 3.4, which leaves little room for a miss. If operating margin fell to 35%, the model value would be 178.34.

decision.timing: The swing target sits well inside the 2026-12-18 options window, which prices a 9.3% move. Any swing position should be closed before the 2027-01-27 report, which the 2027-02-19 options price at a 15.4% move. Long-term money beyond the 475.73 add waits for that report's free cash flow figure.
